eligibility: You self-identify as being from a Black heritage, including mixed Black background.

You are a UK national or you have completed a part of your education in the UK through your Undergraduate, Master's or PhD degree studies or you hold/have held a postdoctoral researcher position in the UK.
You have a PhD, or will have one by the time the funding starts, but have less than 24 months post-doctoral experience.

Your research is within the Royal Society's remit of natural sciences, which includes but is not limited to, biological research and biomedical sciences, chemistry, engineering, mathematics and physics.
Both UK and non-UK domiciled researchers who wish to conduct their research in the UK are eligible.
Applicants can be of any nationality and those requiring a visa are eligible to apply for a Global Talent Visa under the fast-track process of endorsement.
existing.eligibility_summary: Self-identify as being from a Black heritage background, have a UK connection (national, education or a UK postdoc position), hold or be completing a PhD with less than 24 months postdoctoral experience, and work within the Royal Society's natural sciences remit.
benefits: Contribution to the Research Fellow's salary and associated on-costs (at 80%)
Relocation and visa costs for the applicant and their dependants (partner and children), which can be requested in addition to the total grant cap of £703,800 over four years
Financial support for childcare costs arising from attending conferences, collaborative research visits or invited talks

requirements: Apply through Flexi-Grant, the Royal Society application and grant management system
Register interest in the scheme information session
Shortlisted applicants are invited to an in-person interview at the Royal Society
application_method: Choose the Career Development Fellowship scheme for the 2027 round
Complete the application, including research proposal and personal data
Submit before the 18 November 2026 close date
Attend an in-person interview at the Royal Society if shortlisted
existing.selection_notes: Assessment is overseen by the Career Development Fellowship panel. Following the scheme's shortlisting process, shortlisted applicants are invited to an in-person interview at the Royal Society, where the aim is for the applicant to demonstrate the importance and scientific validity of their work. Success rate for 2024/25 was 3% (233 eligible applications, 7 offers).
existing.best_fit: Researchers who self-identify as being from a Black heritage background, including mixed Black background, with fewer than 24 months of postdoctoral experience, who meet the UK connection requirement and want a four-year postdoctoral fellowship in the UK.
existing.notes: This scheme is currently offered as a pilot with researchers from Black heritage backgrounds; if successful, the pilot may be broadened to other underrepresented groups. It is a postdoctoral fellowship for research in the UK, not a degree programme, so it does not pay tuition. Salary and directly allocated costs are paid at 80%, so the host institution must cover part of the cost base. The Royal Society states undergraduate, Master's and PhD students cannot apply for Royal Society funding.
existing.application_period: 2027 round opens 22 September 2026 and closes 18 November 2026; decision by 30 June 2027.
